images.title: The square of 3j + 2k
images.purpose: Shows (3j + 2k)² as a square split into 9j², two 6jk rectangles and 4k², with the two 6jk added to 12jk.
images.composition: One large square centred, split into four parts, with the result underneath. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A large square split in the ratio 3 to 2 along both sides. Top left: a teal (#0072B2) square labelled '9j²'. Top right and bottom left: two amber (#E69F00) rectangles, each labelled '6jk'. Bottom right: a reddish purple (#CC79A7) square labelled '4k²'. Along the top edge, the labels '3j' and '2k' over the two parts. Below the square, centred, the label '9j² + 12jk + 4k²'. Exactly 4 parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Both ways give 9j² + 12jk + 4k², because the two 6jk pieces add to 12jk.
images.description: Shows (3j + 2k)² as a square split into 9j², two 6jk rectangles and 4k², with the two 6jk added to 12jk.

image_decisions.why: The two equal rectangles show why the middle term is 12jk, settling the 6jk or 12jk prediction.
